Selected work

Live in production

Autonomous Customer Support Agent

An agent that reads a support email, works out what the customer needs, pulls relevant knowledge, drafts a reply, checks its own work, and waits for a person to approve before anything goes out.

I built it end to end, from the graph design to deployment, so I can explain every architectural and code-level decision in it.

  • LangGraph
  • Gemini API
  • Postgres + pgvector
  • Supabase
  • FastAPI
  • LangSmith
  • Render
Source on GitHub Live API
  • 10-node agent graph, each node built and tested on its own before being wired together
  • RAG on managed Postgres with pgvector and Gemini embeddings, migrated from a local SQLite and ChromaDB prototype
  • Human-in-the-loop approval through a dedicated API endpoint, so no reply is sent unreviewed
  • Production hardening: retries, safe fallbacks, config validation, and an evaluation suite
  • Next: a web dashboard to submit and track emails, plus a queue for bulk processing, built with a collaborator
Research, co-first author

Can AI run confidentially?

Evaluating local AI for industry applications, Northeastern University, April 2026

Companies with sensitive data want to know whether open models they can run on their own hardware are good enough. We benchmarked open-source LLMs such as LLaMA, Qwen, and DeepSeek against proprietary models like GPT, Claude, and Gemini on MMLU, GPQA, Humanity’s Last Exam, and MedXpertQA.

On saturated benchmarks the two groups perform about the same. On harder, expert-level benchmarks the proprietary models still lead, especially in biomedical and interdisciplinary reasoning. Local models already handle routine work well: summarizing documents, extracting data, reviewing literature, and assisting with code.

  • Co-author, IEEE TEMSMET 2023: real-time smart transformer design based on IoT
  • Research assistant: user research evaluating the usability of digital health education tools

PaveWatch

Dell × NVIDIA Local AI Hackathon, Hult Boston, October 2026

A local agent that tracks road defects from a moving camera. An object detector flags candidate potholes, and a vision-language model looks at each flagged frame to confirm it and describe what it sees.

My part was the vision-language step: running Qwen VLM on the GB10 to classify flagged images as pothole, cracked pavement, or unclear, so only confirmed defects get logged.

Risk factors for diabetes prevalence

Healthcare data study, Northeastern University

A county-level study of U.S. health determinants and how they relate to diabetes prevalence, built on the CDC PLACES 2024 dataset and presented with my team.

Healthcare is where I most want to apply AI, and this study is part of that thread along with my chest X-ray classifier below.
